text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The presidents of Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania are to launch a common passport and plan for closer economic integration in Arusha, Tanzania.
- Members of parliament from the Abagusii community warn the Nyanza provincial administration in western Kenya against undermining them and dividing the community.
- Royal Media Services obtains a government licence to operate a radio and television station in Nairobi.
- The Secretary-General of the opposition FORD-Asili party reiterates the party's stand that it will not endorse national chairman Kenneth Matiba for presidency.
- The ministry of education will soon scrap the ranking of schools in national examinations.
- A background report by the United Nations Centre of Human Settlements says the number of street children in Africa will rise from current 16 million to 30 million by the year 2000.
- The ruling party Kenya African National Union (KANU) warns against a report saying the president had declared the Rift Valley a zone where other parties may not operate.

- Nairobi City Council is losing millions of shillings in water revenue collection after a questionable 8 million shillings contract awarded to a civic leader for the supply of water meters. ($1=55 Kenya Shillings)
